title: introduce-rag-pipeline-dsl-quickstart-with-websocket-tool-bridge-and-replay-harness
author: Avery Chen
release_notes: Add new RAG quickstart demonstrating a lightweight pipeline DSL, websocket tool-bridge for external connectors, replayable session harness, TypeScript and Go worker examples, and devcontainer for local authoring.
description:
Title: Introduce RAG pipeline DSL quickstart with websocket tool-bridge and replay harness

Motivation and context: We have a lot of ad-hoc RAG quickstarts that show tool calling or stepwise orchestration, but teams keep asking for a compact, opinionated example that demonstrates: 1) expressing multi-step RAG flows as a readable pipeline DSL, 2) wiring external connectors via a lightweight websocket tool-bridge (simulates third-party APIs for local dev), 3) deterministic session replay for debugging/evals, and 4) idiomatic worker stubs in TypeScript and Go for integration testing. This PR provides a single quickstart that strings those pieces together so platform teams can onboard quickly and product teams can reproduce noisy production flows locally.

What this PR adds (summary): - A new quickstart directory: quickstarts/rag-pipeline-dsl/ with README, examples, and step templates. - A small pipeline DSL (YAML-first) that maps steps (retrieve -> call -> transform -> assert -> emit) to runtime hooks. The DSL is intentionally tiny (6 primitives) and designed for teaching. - Websocket tool-bridge: lightweight node server that accepts tool calls over websockets to emulate external connectors (search, payment, webhook sink). Includes a small harness to seed deterministic responses. - Replay harness: session serializer + deterministic RNG seeding for replaying a sequence of interactions (useful for CI-evals and debugging flaky prompts). - Two worker stubs: TypeScript (Node) and Go (lightweight HTTP shim) that implement the DSL hooks and demonstrate KV cache hotspots, streaming partial responses, and structured-output enforcement. - Devcontainer + sample k8s manifest for running the quickstart locally or in headless CI. - Telemetry probes: example OpenTelemetry spans and an instrumentation README showing how to add custom metrics to trace step latencies and token counts.

Files touched (high level): - quickstarts/rag-pipeline-dsl/README.md - quickstarts/rag-pipeline-dsl/pipeline-schema.yaml - quickstarts/rag-pipeline-dsl/examples/retail-recommendation.yaml - quickstarts/rag-pipeline-dsl/ws-tool-bridge/ (node websocket server, seeds) - quickstarts/rag-pipeline-dsl/workers/ts-worker/ (npm project with sample handlers) - quickstarts/rag-pipeline-dsl/workers/go-worker/ (go module with http shim) - quickstarts/rag-pipeline-dsl/replay/replay-cli.ts - quickstarts/rag-pipeline-dsl/devcontainer.json - quickstarts/rag-pipeline-dsl/k8s/quickstart.yaml - quickstarts/rag-pipeline-dsl/telemetry/otel-example.md

Commit summary: - 1a2b3c4: initial scaffold and README - 2b3c4d5: add pipeline schema + example flows - 3c4d5e6: websocket tool-bridge implementation + seeds - 4d5e6f7: add TS worker and CI smoke script - 5e6f7g8: add Go worker, k8s manifest, and replay harness - 6f7g8h9: add telemetry probes and docs; fix lint failures - 7g8h9i0: follow-up: update README with troubleshooting and merge prep

Testing and CI: - Unit: TS worker unit tests (Jest) and replay harness tests were added; Go worker has small integration checks. - Smoke: a headless smoke job in CI boots the websocket bridge, runs the dev pipeline against seeded responses, and verifies structured-output assertions pass. - Lint: Prettier/ESLint and gofmt checks.

CI run history on this PR: - Initial run: lint failure (missing gofmt and a couple of ESLint rules) - After fixes: one flaky Jest snapshot for streaming partial responses; reran tests with snapshot update and added an assertion to avoid nondeterministic ordering - Final run: all checks pass (lint/test/smoke)

Review conversation (high level, single thread): - Diego Morales (reviewer): "Nice compact DSL. Two asks: 1) make the structured-output contract explicit in the schema so teams can opt into strict validation, 2) clarify security implications of websocket bridge (seeds may contain secrets)." - Avery Chen (author): "Thanks — added a 'validation' boolean in pipeline-schema.yaml and moved seeds to a sample-only file under ws-tool-bridge/seeds.example.json; updated README with security guidance." - Priya Kapoor (reviewer): "Can we show a minimal example of migrating an existing step to a canary rollout? Suggest adding a short 'rollout' property in the DSL and a cookbook paragraph." - Avery Chen: "Added rollout property and a cookbook paragraph demonstrating a canary flag (percent-based). Also added a console screenshot for step metrics." - Samir Rao (reviewer): "Telemetry looks fine; please add token count metric per-step. Also, ensure replay harness runs deterministically on CI (seed RNG)." - Avery Chen: "Added token_count gauge example and deterministic RNG seeding in replay-cli; updated smoke job to set REPLAY_SEED. Ready for merge." - Diego Morales: "Approved" - Priya Kapoor: "Approved" - Samir Rao: "Approved with comment noting to monitor telemetry quotas after adoption."

Edge cases and notes: - The websocket tool-bridge is intentionally not production-grade; README warns to not expose it externally and to treat it as a local/dev-only shim. - The pipeline DSL is intentionally conservative and designed for teaching and fast iteration; it is not intended to replace production orchestrators but to act as an ergonomic onboarding artifact. - The replay harness serializes prompts, tool call transcripts, and final outputs; it does not currently record raw model latencies (future work).

Docs and onboarding: - README includes step-by-step guide to run the quickstart locally (devcontainer recommended), how to seed tool responses, and how to run replay and smoke checks. - A short 'migrating from ad-hoc scripts' cookbook paragraph helps platform engineers convert existing one-off scripts to the DSL.

Compatibility and backward compatibility: - Nonbreaking: all files are additive; no changes to runtime or core APIs. - Example flows use public SDK calls to Redwood API; developers will need an API key to run the flow against hosted models (instructions in README explain using sandbox mode with the websocket bridge).

Merge outcome: - Squash-merged to main on 2025-01-17 by Diego Morales. Commit message: "quickstarts(rag): add pipeline DSL quickstart + websocket tool-bridge + replay harness" Commit SHA (squash): 9a8b7c6d9f0e1a2b3c4d5e6f7g8h9i0j

Follow-ups (suggested): - ENG-2410: Integrate pipeline DSL examples into docs site as an interactive notebook. - ENG-2421: Add a 'live playback' web UI for replayed sessions (could extend websocket bridge). - PM-159: Track adoption in on-call rotations and sample teams for feedback.

Checklist (from PR description): - [x] Quickstart scaffolded and README - [x] Pipeline schema + sample flows - [x] Websocket tool-bridge + seeds - [x] TypeScript and Go worker stubs - [x] Replay harness and deterministic seed support - [x] Devcontainer + k8s manifest - [x] Telemetry probes and example docs - [x] CI smoke job and lint fixes

If you want to run locally: git clone .../redwood-quickstarts && cd quickstarts/rag-pipeline-dsl && ./dev/run-local.sh (devcontainer recommended).
